knowledge:
- key_parameters: k.titration=A vector of k values to test for neighborhood size optimization in ImputeTesting ;; k=Number of nearest neighbors in Fnn, recommended default is total cells / 100 ;; unstim=The name of the baseline/unstimulated condition in SconeValues ;; numcells=Number of cells to subsample before running t-SNE in SubsampleAndTsne ;; tsne=Logical flag in PostProcessing indicating whether to run t-SNE (set to FALSE for large datasets)
- alternatives: Quantile normalization and z-score transformation are mentioned as preprocessing steps to reduce technical variation before running Sconify.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for flow and mass cytometry (CyTOF) data to assess technical variation, evaluate normalization quality, perform differential abundance/expression analysis, and visualize single-cell functional marker changes on t-SNE maps.
- pitfalls: Running t-SNE on large datasets (>100K cells) is time-consuming and produces less clean results; users should subsample first using SubsampleAndTsne or set tsne = FALSE in PostProcessing. Selecting a sub-optimal k can affect the bias-variance tradeoff, though slight variations around the ideal k typically do not change the output substantially.

workflows.name: scone_differential_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform KNN-based differential expression and abundance analysis on CyTOF data, including neighborhood size optimization, statistical testing, t-SNE visualization, and quality assessment.
input: markers.csv (CSV file containing static and functional marker classifications)
cell_data.csv (or R data frame of concatenated single-cell expression data across conditions)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse marker classifications into input (static) and functional markers using ParseMarkers ;; 2. Optimize the neighborhood size parameter k using ImputeTesting ;; 3. Generate the k-nearest neighbor matrix using Fnn ;; 4. Compute fold changes and statistical significance (q-values) per KNN using SconeValues ;; 5. Merge Scone statistics with original cell data and compute t-SNE coordinates using PostProcessing (or SubsampleAndTsne for large datasets) ;; 6. Visualize results using MakeHist and TsneVis ;; 7. Optionally extract KNN lists or density estimations using MakeKnnList and GetKnnDe
workflows.code:
marker.file <- system.file('extdata', 'markers.csv', package = "Sconify")
markers <- ParseMarkers(marker.file)
input.markers <- markers[[1]]
funct.markers <- markers[[2]]
wand.k.titration <- 1 : 100 %>% .[. %% 10 == 0 ]
wand.ideal.k <- ImputeTesting ( k.titration = wand.k.titration, cells = wand.il7, input.markers = input.markers, test.markers = funct.markers)
k <- 30
wand.nn <- Fnn(cell.df = wand.combined, input.markers = input.markers, k = k)
wand.scone <- SconeValues(nn.matrix = wand.nn, cell.data = wand.combined, scone.markers = funct.markers, unstim = "basal")
wand.final <- PostProcessing ( scone.output = wand.scone, cell.data = wand.combined, input = input.markers)
wand.final.sub <- SubsampleAndTsne ( dat = wand.final, input = input.markers, numcells = 500 )
MakeHist (wand.final, 30 , "IL7.fraction.cond.2" , "fraction IL7" )
TsneVis (wand.final, "IgM(Eu153)Di" , "Raw IgM expression" )
TsneVis (wand.final, "IL7.fraction.cond.2" , "Fraction cells in Il7 condition" )
TsneVis (wand.final, "pSTAT5(Nd150)Di.IL7.change" , "IL7 -> pSTAT5 change" )
TsneVis (wand.final, "pSTAT5(Nd150)Di.IL7.qvalue" , "IL7 -> pSTAT5 -log10(qvalue)" )
TsneVis (wand.final, "density" )
wand.knn.list <- MakeKnnList(cell.data = wand.combined, nn.matrix = wand.nn)
wand.knn.density <- GetKnnDe(nn.matrix = wand.nn)
